newsitem.title: INDIA: India seen second-biggest cement producer by 2000.
newsitem.headline: India seen second-biggest cement producer by 2000.

text.p: India's plans to boost its cement-making capacity over the next few years could make it the world's largest cement producer after China by 2000, Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said on Tuesday.

"The Indian cement industry is (currently) the fourth biggest in the world and by around the turn of the century, we may become the second biggest, (edging past Japan and the United States)," Maran told a seminar on cement and building materials.
Maran said India's cement industry was expanding rapidly and was modernising to satisfy growing demand for cement from the power and infrastructure sectors.
India produced 69.31 million tonnes of cement during fiscal 1995/96 (April-March), according to official figures.

"Due to massive modernisation and the expansion programme undertaken by the cement industry, cement production is going to touch 100 million tonnes by 2000 as against hardly 30 million tonnes in the early 1980s," Maran said.
India currently has an annual capacity of 94 million tonnes, but produces about 70 million tonnes annually, against an annual consumption of nearly 63 million tonnes of cement.
Maran said India produced just over 60 million tonnes with "state of the art" techniques. "There still remains eight to 10 million tonnes of capacity based on obsolete technology," he added.
